title: Past perfect simple, past perfect continuous
subtitle: Actions finished or continuing before another moment in the past

rows.person: I / you / he / she / it / we / they
rows.question: **Had** I/you/he/she/it/we/they **written** …?

rows.use: Actions and states before a moment in the past
rows.example: I'd **finished** my homework a few minutes before the lesson started.

rows.use: Finished actions and states where the important thing is the result at a moment in the past
rows.example: We were happy because we'd **all done** our homework.

blocks.intro: The past perfect simple is often used with these words and phrases:
items: {pill:by} — I'd finished my homework **by** eight o'clock.
{pill:by the time} — **By the time** I got to class, the lesson had started.
{pill:before} — The teacher had checked the answers **before** the lesson.
{pill:after} — I left **after** I'd finished the test.
{pill:just} — Simon had **just** finished the test when the bell rang.
{pill:when} — I left **when** I'd finished the test.

blocks.text: Whether we use the past simple or the past perfect simple can change the meaning of a sentence.
blocks.note: The lesson **started** when I arrived. (= I arrived and then the lesson started.) · The lesson **had started** when I arrived. (= The lesson started and then I arrived.)

rows.person: I / you / he / she / it / we / they
rows.question: **Had** I/you/he/she/it/we/they **been writing** …?

rows.use: Actions continuing up to, or stopping just before, a moment in the past
rows.example: We'd **been doing** grammar exercises for over an hour, so we were really bored!

blocks.intro: The past perfect continuous is often used with these words and phrases:
items: {pill:for} — Tony had been studying **for** hours, so he had a headache.
{pill:since} — She'd been hoping to win the competition **since** the summer.
{pill:before} — We'd been talking about the Internet **before** the lesson started.
{pill:all day} / {pill:all night} — I'd been studying **all day**.

blocks.text: The past perfect simple often emphasises the **result** of an action.
blocks.note: She'd **written** an article for the school newspaper. (= She'd finished it.)

blocks.text: The past perfect continuous often emphasises the **action** and the time spent on it, rather than the result.
blocks.note: She'd **been writing** an article for the newspaper. (= She'd started, but she hadn't finished it.)

exercises.title: A · Past perfect simple
exercises.instruction: Complete using the correct past perfect simple form of the verbs in brackets.

items.prompt: By the time I arrived, everyone ___ ! (leave)
Steve ___ the film, so he didn't come with us to the cinema. (already / see)
Tina ___ doing the housework by seven o'clock, so she called Andrea to tell her she would be late. (not / finish)
___ to Billy when I rang? (you / just / speak)
The car broke down just after we ___ . (set off)
I didn't eat anything at the party because I ___ at home. (already / eat)
___ about the accident before you saw it on TV? (you / hear)

exercises.title: B · Same meaning?
exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence (A or B) which means the same as the first sentence.

items.prompt: We'd had dinner when Wendy arrived.
options: Wendy arrived and then we had dinner.
We had dinner and then Wendy arrived.
acceptedAnswers: We had dinner and then Wendy arrived.

items.prompt: I read the book after I'd seen the film.
options: I saw the film and then I read the book.
I read the book and then I saw the film.
acceptedAnswers: I saw the film and then I read the book.

items.prompt: By the time Dad came home, I'd gone to bed.
options: I went to bed before Dad came home.
I went to bed after Dad came home.
acceptedAnswers: I went to bed before Dad came home.

items.prompt: She didn't go to bed until her mum had come home.
options: She went to bed and then her mum came home.
Her mum came home and then she went to bed.
acceptedAnswers: Her mum came home and then she went to bed.

items.prompt: Mr Banks hadn't arrived at the office by the time I got there.
They'd bought the plane tickets before they heard about the cheaper flight.
options: They bought the plane tickets and later they heard about the cheaper flight.
They heard about the cheaper flight and then they bought the plane tickets.
acceptedAnswers: They bought the plane tickets and later they heard about the cheaper flight.

items.prompt: The girls had tidied the house when the visitors arrived.
options: The visitors arrived and later the girls tidied the house.
The girls tidied the house and then the visitors arrived.
acceptedAnswers: The girls tidied the house and then the visitors arrived.

exercises.title: C · Write a sentence
exercises.instruction: Write sentences using the prompts. One of the verbs must be in the past perfect simple.

items.prompt: we / just / hear / the news / when / you / ring
acceptedAnswers: We'd just heard the news when you rang.
We'd just heard the news when you rang
We had just heard the news when you rang.
We had just heard the news when you rang

items.prompt: I / already / think of / that / before / you / suggest / it
acceptedAnswers: I'd already thought of that before you suggested it.
I'd already thought of that before you suggested it
I had already thought of that before you suggested it.
I had already thought of that before you suggested it

items.prompt: when / I / turn on / the TV / the programme / already / start
acceptedAnswers: When I turned on the TV, the programme had already started.
When I turned on the TV, the programme had already started
When I turned on the TV the programme had already started.
When I turned on the TV the programme had already started

items.prompt: she / be / hungry / because / she / not / eat / anything / all day
acceptedAnswers: She was hungry because she hadn't eaten anything all day.
She was hungry because she hadn't eaten anything all day
She was hungry because she had not eaten anything all day.
She was hungry because she had not eaten anything all day

items.prompt: by the time / I / leave / school / I / decide / to become / a musician
acceptedAnswers: By the time I left school, I had decided to become a musician.
By the time I left school, I had decided to become a musician
By the time I left school I'd decided to become a musician.
By the time I left school I'd decided to become a musician
By the time I left school, I'd decided to become a musician.
By the time I left school, I'd decided to become a musician

exercises.title: D · Picture stories
exercises.instruction: Complete the sentences using the past perfect continuous.

items.prompt: She was tired because she ___ . (run)
They were hot because they ___ . (dance)
The garden was flooded because it ___ all night. (rain)
Did they crash because they ___ too fast? (drive)
When I arrived, they ___ for over half an hour. (wait)
When I got there, they ___ long. (not / wait)

exercises.title: E · Choose the correct answer
exercises.instruction: Select the form that completes each sentence.

items.prompt: I'd only ___ the washing-up for a few minutes when Clare came home, so she offered to finish it.
Had you already ___ James his birthday present when we gave him ours?
Gail hadn't ___ me that she would help me, so I wasn't angry when she didn't.
Mum had ___ her cup of tea for several minutes before she realised it had salt in it!
We'd ___ ready all day when they called to say the party had been cancelled.
It was a fantastic experience because I'd never ___ in a plane before.

exercises.title: F · Exam-results diary
exercises.instruction: Tap the verb that is wrong, then write the correct form.
exercises.paragraph: This morning my exam results finally {click:had came}. I'd been expecting them for the last week. I knew I'd {click:been done} quite well, but I was still nervous as I {click:had opened} the envelope. Before I'd had a chance to look at them, my sister ran up and pulled them out of my hand! She {click:had read} them out one by one. 'English A, maths A, biology A, French A …' This was the news I'd been waiting for. I'd got As in every subject — even geography, which I {click:hadn't been making} sure about! When Mum and Dad heard the news, they immediately started shouting with joy. By the time I'd had breakfast, Mum had already called Grandma and Grandpa and {click:had yet told} the neighbours!

items.prompt: Completed event this morning
items.explanation: A finished event at a stated time uses the past simple, not past perfect. Also come → came, not came after had.

items.prompt: Result, not a process
items.explanation: I'd done quite well = result. Extra been is wrong.

items.prompt: Main story event
items.explanation: The nervous moment of opening the envelope is a past simple event in the story.

items.prompt: Sequence of events
items.explanation: She read them out after taking them — next event, not earlier background.

items.prompt: State, not an activity
items.explanation: Use a state: I hadn't been sure about it. Extra making is wrong.

items.prompt: Extra time word
items.explanation: yet does not belong here. Use past perfect without yet: had told.
